players.attrWhy: 36-yr-old ex-Leverkusen title-winning keeper; reliable shot-stopper, calm with feet, declining agility

players.name: Vanderson
players.attrWhy: Brazil-capped RB; explosive, strong in duels, attacking runs; crossing and decisions inconsistent

players.name: Sané
players.attrWhy: Sadibou Sané, 21-22, €10m from relegated Metz (23 L1 apps, 2 goals 25/26); physical, still raw

players.name: Dier
players.attrWhy: 32-yr-old ex-Bayern CB; good passer and reader of play, strong in the air, very slow

players.name: Nazinho
players.attrWhy: Flávio Nazinho, 22, €5m from Cercle Brugge (3G 8A in 32 apps 25/26); attacking LB, step up from Belgium

players.name: Camara
players.attrWhy: Lamine Camara, Senegal international; ball-winner with good press resistance and long passing

players.name: Zakaria
players.attrWhy: Switzerland captain-level DM; powerful box-to-box runner, strong duels, tidy rather than creative

players.name: Coulibaly
players.attrWhy: Mamadou Coulibaly, a natural DM used on the right wing in 26/27; work rate and duels over flair

players.name: Golovin
players.attrWhy: Creative hub; elite vision and passing at L1 level, set up both goals at PSG; injury-prone and aging

players.name: Idumbo
players.attrWhy: Stanis Idumbo, ex-Sevilla; quick 1v1 dribbler, limited output in 25/26 (1G 1A, few minutes)

players.name: Brunner
players.attrWhy: Paris Brunner, 20; 4 L1 goals in 26/27 after a goalless 25/26; mobile, strong target forward

clubs.tacticsWhy: Possession (Footmercato/foot-direct, psg.fr): 50% at Le Havre, 36% vs Marseille, 33% at PSG, 56% at Strasbourg, 50% vs Lens, 58% vs Toulouse. That averages about 47%, and the two biggest wins (2-0 vs OM, 2-1 at PSG) came with only a third of the ball. At PSG both goals came from fast transitions: Golovin won the ball and sent Idumbo through, then Golovin switched play to Coulibaly, whose cross found Nazinho (psg.fr live). So tempo 4 and passing 3. Width 3: wide midfielders Coulibaly and Idumbo, with full-back Nazinho arriving from the far side. No PPDA or line-height metric was found, so press 3 and line 3 are neutral. Style 'normal' (10 scored, 5 conceded in 6). No set-piece source, so setAtt/setDef are placeholders.
clubs.desc: Monaco står kompakt i en 4-2-3-1 med to defensive midtbanespillere, kan sagtens overlade bolden til modstanderen og er farligst i hurtige omstillinger, hvor den kreative tier og kanterne spiller hurtigt frem mod angriberen.
uncertain: Shirt numbers: Footmercato's lineup box and the main AS Monaco FC Wikipedia page (squad as of 9 Sep 2026) give Dier 15 and Camara 8. The 2026–27 season page (as of 2 Sep) gives Dier 3 and Camara 15. I used 15 and 8.
Sides of the double pivot conflict. Footmercato/foot-direct list Zakaria left and Camara right; psg.fr's order suggests the reverse.

Absence reasons for Toulouse (Brunner suspended, Coulibaly with an adductor problem) come from a search summary of africafootunited.com that I did not fetch. The Toulouse XI was Hrádecký; Vanderson, Sané, Dier, Nazinho; Zakaria, Camara; Detourbet, Golovin, E. Diop; Abline. It drew 2-2 in a 4-2-3-1.
Start counts: Hrádecký, Vanderson, Sané, Dier, Nazinho, Zakaria, Camara and Golovin 6; Brunner 5; Idumbo 4; Coulibaly 3. Monaco played a 4-4-2 vs Lens (Diop, Abline in).

clubs.tacticsWhy: Possession (foot-direct): 52% at Toulouse, 57% vs Le Havre, 64% vs Auxerre, 44% at Paris FC, 45% vs Rennes, 52% at Lens. That averages about 52%, so passing 3 and tempo 3. Results are efficient rather than dominant: 4-0 vs Rennes with 45% of the ball and 15 shots to 6, 0-0 at Paris FC with 2 shots, and 8 shots to 15 in the 2-1 loss at Lens. Lyon scored 11 and conceded 4 in 6. Full-back Athekame scored twice (vs Auxerre and Rennes), so the full-backs push on; width 3. Fonseca called Lyon 'une équipe d'initiative' before Lens (Ferveur Lyonnaise), but no PPDA or line-height metric was found, so press 3 and line 3 are neutral. Style 'normal'. No set-piece source, so setAtt/setDef are placeholders.
clubs.desc: Lyon spiller en balanceret og initiativrig 4-3-3 med en arbejdsom midtbane på tre, offensive backer, der også dukker op foran mål, og hurtige angribere i front.
uncertain: Formation labels conflict. Footmercato and foot-direct say 4-3-3 for 9 Oct; Fox Sports says 4-2-3-1; Foot01 groups the XI as Morton, Bidstrup, Tolisso, Šulc – Nuamah, Openda (diamond-like). The same data provider labelled the three previous matches with this core XI as 4-3-2-1, 4-2-3-1 and 4-2-3-1.

Front-three roles: Footmercato's 19 Sep text puts Openda through the middle with Nuamah and Šulc wide, which I used. The 9 Oct data order (Openda, Šulc, Nuamah) could instead mean Šulc central. Midfield sides follow the data order (Tolisso left, Morton centre, Bidstrup right).

The XI was kept even though Niakhaté (19) was injured and Kluivert replaced him at centre-back, because it was the only change. Otherwise the XI is identical to 4 Sep vs Auxerre, 12 Sep at Paris FC and 19 Sep vs Rennes. Openda went off injured during the Lens match.
The opening match at Toulouse (22 Aug) was a heavily rotated XI, three days before the UCL play-off vs Fenerbahçe, and is not representative.

clubs.tacticsWhy: Possession (foot-direct/Footmercato): 67% vs Strasbourg, 64% at Monaco, 61% vs Paris FC, 51% at Rennes, 39% vs PSG, 63% at Troyes. That averages about 57%, so the side is possession-based. Centre-back pass volumes were very high (Aguerd 93/95 vs Paris FC, Egan-Riley 115/121 at Troyes), which points to a short, patient build-up: passing 2, tempo 2. Yet OM lost 2-0 at Monaco with 64% of the ball and 3-2 to Paris FC with 61%, so they do not dominate in the box. Style 'normal'. No PPDA or line-height data was found, so press 3 and line 3 are neutral. Width 3: Paixão holds the left, Harit comes inside from the right, and Emerson made 3 successful crosses/corners at Rennes. No set-piece source, so setAtt/setDef are placeholders.

clubs.tacticsWhy: Possession in the 6 league games (foot-direct/Footmercato match data): 69% at Rennes, 73% at Lille, 67% vs Monaco, 59% at Brest, 61% at Marseille, 73% vs Le Mans. That averages about 67%, the highest of the four clubs, so passing 1 (short) and tempo 3 (patient circulation but fast wide players). Shots 21 v 12 at Marseille and 22 v 14 vs Le Mans (attributed by column order), so style 'off'. Monaco's two goals at the Parc came from quick transitions behind the PSG defence (psg.fr live), which fits a high line: line 5. No PPDA or line-height metric was found for 2026/27, so press 5 is a judgement from Luis Enrique's high-pressing positional game, not a measured stat. Width 4: wingers Doué and Kvaratskhelia play wide and full-backs Hakimi and Mendes push on. No set-piece source, so setAtt/setDef are placeholders.
